_comment: One entry per real data source used in the pipeline. Appended to as each phase downloads something — do not hand-edit the auto-filled fields (sha256, downloadDate) without re-running the download.

sources.name: VG250 Verwaltungsgebiete 1:250 000 — Kreise (districts)
sources.processingNotes: Filtered to AGS starting '09' (Bavaria, 96 districts), reprojected EPSG:25832 -> EPSG:4326, simplified (tolerance 0.005°, preserve_topology=True) for web use.

sources.name: Austria Bezirke (district) boundaries, 2021, simplified 99.5%
sources.provider: Flooh Perlot (processed), original data Statistik Austria
sources.attribution: Flooh Perlot / Statistik Austria (data.statistik.gv.at), CC BY 4.0
sources.processedOutput: not yet processed — archived raw only in Phase 2; app still fetches live from GitHub until the switch is made
sources.processingNotes: 117 features (all Austrian districts, not pre-filtered to Upper Austria). Previously fetched live at runtime from this same URL in BavariaHeatmap.tsx (AUSTRIA_DISTRICTS_URL) — now archived locally; app code not yet switched over.

sources.name: HYRAS-DE v6-1 — monthly mean air temperature (tas)
sources.license: DWD Open Data (GeoNutzV / CC BY 4.0 equivalent)
sources.crs: EPSG:3035 (verified directly from the NetCDF crs variable attrs, not assumed from documentation)
sources.processedOutput: public/data/districts-climate.json (tasMean, tasAnomaly); also public/data/towns-climate.json (Phase 4 — nearest-grid-cell point extraction per Bavarian town, not zonal, via process_town_climate.py)
sources.processingNotes: Zonal mean per VG250 Bavaria district via rasterstats default method (pixel-CENTER-in-polygon, not fractional-area weighting — see processing script docstring). Source y-axis is stored ascending (non-standard); .sortby('y', ascending=False) applied before computing the affine transform, otherwise rasterstats raises or silently mis-indexes. tasAnomaly computed vs. each district's own 1961-1990 mean. Verified against DWD's official Bayern regional average (opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/regional_averages_DE/annual/air_temperature_mean/): an AREA-WEIGHTED district mean (weight = district polygon area in EPSG:3035) matches DWD within -0.043°C mean difference (std 0.014°C, 1951-2024) — an UNWEIGHTED mean overstates Bavaria-wide temperature by +0.116°C because Bavaria's 25 small, warm, urban Kreisfreie Städte then count equally against much larger rural Landkreise. The app's per-district values themselves are unaffected by this (each district shows its own real value); only a Bavaria-wide aggregate, if ever computed in the UI, should use the area-weighted method.

sources.name: HYRAS-DE v6-1 — monthly precipitation sum (pr)
sources.license: DWD Open Data (GeoNutzV / CC BY 4.0 equivalent)
sources.periodCovered: File named 1931-2024; actual first timestamp verified directly from the NetCDF time coordinate is 1930-01 (1140 months total). 1930-1950 kept only for SPI-12 lead-in/calibration; the app displays 1951-2024.
sources.processingNotes: Same zonal-mean method and y-axis fix as tas. SPI-12 (December value = calendar-year state) and SPI-3 (August value = JJA summer state) computed per district with climate-indices v2.2.0, gamma distribution, calibrated 1961-1990. droughtClass thresholds: D0 ≤ -0.5, D1 ≤ -0.8, D2 ≤ -1.3, D3 ≤ -1.6, D4 ≤ -2.0 (standard SPI/USDM convention). Sanity-checked: 2003 and 2018 both show widespread drought (2003 mean SPI-12 = -1.96, 96/96 districts in drought; 2018 mean SPI-12 = -1.31, 84/96 districts); 2002 and 1965 both show widespread wet conditions (mean SPI-12 = +1.85 and +1.70 respectively), confirming the index isn't just always negative.

sources.name: DWD grids_germany — annual hot days (Tmax ≥ 30°C)
sources.license: DWD Open Data (GeoNutzV / CC BY 4.0 equivalent)
sources.version: 1km ESRI ASCII grid product (not HYRAS — a separate DWD gridding method; documented here so it isn't mistaken for a HYRAS-derived figure)
variables: hot days per year (count of days with Tmax ≥ 30°C)
sources.crs: EPSG:31467 (Gauss-Krüger zone 3 — verified by reprojecting the grid bounds to WGS84 and checking against Germany's known extent, not assumed)
sources.processedOutput: public/data/districts-climate.json (hotDays, per-district area mean); also public/data/towns-climate.json (Phase 4 — nearest-grid-cell point value per Bavarian town, not an area mean)
sources.processingNotes: -999 = NODATA. Zonal mean per district (same rasterstats pixel-center method as tas/pr), districts reprojected to EPSG:31467 separately from the EPSG:3035 geometry used for tas/pr. Sanity-checked: Bavaria-wide top 5 years by mean hot days are 2015 (25.8), 2003 (24.9), 2018 (19.2), 1994 (17.8), 2022 (16.8) — matches the historically documented hottest German summers.

sources.name: SPARTACUS v2.1 — monthly mean temperature (TM) and precipitation sum (RR)
sources.version: v2.1 (flagged deprecated in favor of a v3 endpoint by the provider as of download date; v2.1 used since it was the stable endpoint verified working)
sources.periodCovered: 1961-2024 — SPARTACUS has NO coverage before 1961; 1951-1960 is genuinely absent for Austria, not filled or estimated
sources.rawFiles: data/raw/geosphere-spartacus/tm/spartacus_TM_<start>_<end>.nc and .../rr/spartacus_RR_<start>_<end>.nc (22+22 files, 3-year chunks — the API's grid-slice endpoint caps requests at 10,000,000 data points, which a 3-year/36-month chunk at this grid size stays under)
sources.crs: EPSG:3416 (ETRS89 / Austria Lambert — stated directly in the NetCDF crs attribute)
sources.processedOutput: public/data/austria-districts-climate.json; also public/data/towns-climate.json (Phase 4 — nearest-grid-cell point extraction per Austria town, from each town's own real station start year, not SPARTACUS's blanket 1961)
sources.processingNotes: Same SPI-12/SPI-3 method and droughtClass thresholds as the Bavaria HYRAS pipeline, calibrated 1961-1990 (the full available baseline, since data starts exactly then). Per-chunk files are concatenated along time before zonal statistics; this surfaced a second, deeper variant of the HYRAS y-axis bug — after concat+resort, rioxarray's cached affine transform goes stale and silently reverts to a positive-dy (south-up) orientation even though the y coordinate itself is correctly ordered, so .rio.transform(recalc=True) is required on every zonal_stats call here (not just a one-time .sortby fix). Verified directly by comparing the raw y-coordinate order against the transform's sign before trusting it. No DWD-equivalent hot-days product exists for Austria in this pipeline; hotDays is null for all Austria districts/years. Upper Austria district boundaries: the 18 Bezirke already archived in Phase 2 (data/raw/austria/bezirke_995_geo.json), filtered by iso code prefix '4' and reprojected to EPSG:3416.

sources.name: GeoSphere Austria station climatology — daily (klima-v2-1d)
sources.periodCovered: Per-station real coverage, verified directly against this endpoint's own metadata (not assumed): Linz (56) since 1895-07-01, Braunau/Ranshofen (75) since 1961-01-01, Wels-Schleißheim (4905) since 1983-10-01, Salzburg Freisaal (145) since 1987-01-01
variables: rr (daily precipitation, -1 = no precipitation not missing)
sources.accessMethod: Two uses: (1) this Python pipeline fetches tlmax live via requests (no CORS concern offline) to count real hot days (Tmax >= 30°C) per year per town, output into public/data/towns-climate.json; (2) the running app's own browser fetches (src/hooks/useAustriaData.ts) use the same endpoint live, with all 4 parameters, as the primary source for the Town-climate scroll story for Austrian towns, falling back to Open-Meteo only on a GeoSphere error and only for years within the station's own real coverage (see noSilentMixing method note)
sources.processedOutput: public/data/towns-climate.json (Austria towns' hotDays field, real daily tlmax >= 30°C counts — a point station measurement, not a gridded product, since no DWD-equivalent hot-days grid exists for Austria)
sources.processingNotes: Fetched in <=20-year chunks per station to keep individual requests small; stationStartYear values also hardcoded into AUSTRIA_TOWNS in geoData.ts so the live app can clip its own requests the same way.

sources.name: Linz / Donau — daily mean water level (W-Tagesmittel)
sources.license: eHYD Nutzungsbedingungen (CC BY 4.0, per Phase 5a research)
sources.periodCovered: 1921-01-01 to 2024-01-01 (37,621 daily rows, 129 marked Lücke/gap, 37,492 real values)
variables: Wasserstand (daily mean water level), cm, relative to the gauge zero valid at each date
sources.encoding: ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1), CRLF line endings — verified directly (ß/ü/ö decode correctly), not assumed from docs
sources.processingNotes: Gauge zero changed 3 times (see Stammdaten entry) — 1821: 250.83 m ü.A., 1939-11-01: 247.83 m ü.A., 1959-01-01: 247.74 m ü.A. Also: per the file's own Anmerkungen, the gauge has been in the backwater/reservoir zone of the Donau-Kraftwerk Abwinden-Asten dam since 1979 — water levels from 1979 onward are regulated, not a free-flowing natural river level, a significant caveat for any drought/low-water interpretation across that boundary.

sources.name: Linz / Donau — station master data (Stammdaten)
sources.license: eHYD Nutzungsbedingungen (CC BY 4.0, per Phase 5a research)
variables: Anmerkungen (footnotes), including the 1979 dam backwater note
sources.processedOutput: gauge-zero history table used by process_gauges.py (Phase 5b) to decide where a continuous series is valid vs. where the datum must be cut

sources.name: Linz / Donau — monthly maximum water level (W-Monatsmaxima)
sources.license: eHYD Nutzungsbedingungen (CC BY 4.0, per Phase 5a research)
variables: Wasserstand (monthly maximum, from the same daily-mean series), cm — timestamp given is the day within that month the maximum occurred
sources.processedOutput: cross-check only (Phase 5b 5b-3) against our own computed annual maxima from the daily series — not used as a primary data source

methodNotes.areaWeighting: Per-district values in districts-climate.json and austria-districts-climate.json are each district's own zonal statistic — no aggregation across districts happens in the pipeline output. If the app or a future chart computes a Bavaria-wide (or Upper-Austria-wide) aggregate from these per-district values, it MUST be area-weighted (weight = district polygon area), not a plain mean — verified directly: an unweighted mean of the 96 Bavaria districts' tasMean overstates the true Bavaria-wide annual temperature by +0.116°C on average (std 0.014°C) vs. DWD's own official regional average, because Bavaria's 25 small, warm, urban Kreisfreie Städte would otherwise count equally against much larger rural Landkreise. Area-weighting brings the difference to -0.043°C (std 0.014°C), matching DWD within its own method's expected tolerance.
methodNotes.hotDaysMethod: hotDays in districts-climate.json comes from DWD's own ready-made grids_germany/annual/hot_days product (EPSG:31467, 1km, Tmax ≥ 30°C day counts), NOT derived from HYRAS daily tasmax — HYRAS daily data was never downloaded for this pipeline (see Phase 1 decision 4). This is a DIFFERENT DWD gridding method/product than the HYRAS-DE tas/pr grids used for temperature and drought in the same file, included here so a reader doesn't assume hotDays shares HYRAS's provenance, resolution, or exact methodology.
methodNotes.spiToDroughtIndexMapping: BavariaHeatmap.tsx maps real SPI-12 onto the pre-existing 0..1 'drought index' scale that DROUGHT_THRESHOLDS/droughtThresholdColor (and the unchanged legend) expect, via a PIECEWISE-linear function (not a single linear fit), so each D-class boundary lands exactly on the corresponding existing UI tier boundary: SPI -0.5 (D0) -> 0.32 'Abnormally dry', -0.8 (D1) -> 0.40 'Dry', -1.3 (D2) -> 0.47 'Drought', -1.6 (D3) -> 0.54 'Severe', -2.0 (D4) -> 0.61 'Extreme'. The D-classes are NOT evenly spaced in SPI (D0-D1 spans 0.3, D1-D2 spans 0.5, D2-D3 spans 0.3, D3-D4 spans 0.4), which is why a single linear fit across the whole range cannot hit all five at once — the single-linear version used during initial Phase 3 approval only approximately matched the first and last anchors. There is no further real D-class boundary beyond D4 to anchor the sixth tier ('Critical', 0.69) to, so it's reached by continuing the D3->D4 segment's own rate rather than a separately chosen cutoff (works out to SPI ≈ -2.46). Wetter than -0.5 (not in any D-class) always floors to exactly 0 before any decade-averaging — the single-linear version did not floor non-drought years to 0 first, which let them contribute small positive fractions into decadeAvg.spi12 averages and measurably inflated the apparent severity of decades with few real dry years (e.g. the 2010s' decade-average mis-colored as widespread mild drought across nearly the whole region); the piecewise version fixes this as a side effect of anchoring correctly.
methodNotes.noDataRendering: District/year combinations with no real data at all (Bavaria: 1950, one year before HYRAS coverage starts in 1951; Upper Austria: 1951-1960, before SPARTACUS coverage starts in 1961) are a distinct NO_DATA sentinel (-999, exported from BavariaHeatmap.tsx), not 0/transparent — 0 means 'real data, no drought/no anomaly this year', which is a different, equally real statement. NO_DATA renders as a solid light grey fill (NO_DATA_FILL_COLOR, #969696 in the legend) on both the drought and climate-anomaly layers, with a 'No data' row added to both legends (ColorLegend.tsx / getColorLegend in colorScales.ts) — the only existing-legend content change in this pass, both explicitly requested. True diagonal-hatch fill was considered but needs deck.gl's FillStyleExtension (a new dependency plus a pattern texture atlas) — out of scope for this prototype pass; solid grey was used instead and is flagged here as a possible later upgrade, not a silent simplification. getDecadeAvg returns NO_DATA only when EVERY year in the requested range is missing (e.g. Upper Austria's 1950s decade); a partially-covered decade (e.g. Bavaria's 1950s, 9 of 10 years real) still returns a real average over just the valid years, per the existing averaging fix from Phase 3 approval.
methodNotes.hotspotRule: A district is flagged as a drought hotspot (gold border + % label on the map) if its real SPI-12 record was in at least D0 'abnormally dry' drought (index > 0.32, i.e. SPI-12 ≤ -0.5) for MORE than 30% of the years 1950-2024 (NO_DATA years never count toward this), ranked by that percentage and capped to the worst 5 Bavaria districts / 1 Upper Austria district. Recalibrated from the prior synthetic generator's '>50% of years in severe drought' rule, which is unreachable with real data — the real maximum across all 96 Bavaria districts is exactly 50.0% (Kaufbeuren), so `minPct` was lowered to 0.30; `topK`, not `minPct`, is what actually bounds the result in practice (comfortably below the top 5-10 districts' real 0.35-0.50 range and above the Bavaria-wide mean of ~0.30).
methodNotes.spiD1ShareByDecade: decadeAvg.<decade>.spiD1Share (both districts-climate.json and austria-districts-climate.json) is the share of years in that decade with SPI-12 <= -0.8 (D1, moderate drought or worse), over years with real data only (a missing year is excluded from the denominator, not counted as 'not dry'); null if the decade has zero real years. Computed per the user's request to evaluate as a candidate alternative to decadeAvg.spi12 for the split-map (1950s vs 2010s) view, since a straight decade-averaged SPI washes out single sharp dry years (e.g. 2015, 2018) against several wetter years in the same decade — verified directly: Linz's (iso 401) decade-average spi12 for the 2010s is only -0.32 (barely visible on the drought scale), while its spiD1Share for the same decade is 0.30 (3 of 10 years in at least moderate drought), a much more legible signal. NOT wired into the UI yet — the field exists in the JSON for evaluation only, pending a decision on whether to use it in place of decadeAvg.spi12 for the split map.
methodNotes.townWarmingTrendMethod: BAVARIAN_TOWNS/AUSTRIA_TOWNS.warming (geoData.ts) is an OLS linear-trend total change (numpy polyfit degree 1, slope * (last_year - first_year)), not a raw first-year-vs-last-year difference, computed from HYRAS tas (Bavaria) or SPARTACUS TM (Austria) at the single 1km grid cell nearest each town's coordinates — a POINT extraction, not the area-weighted zonal mean used for districts, so a town's warming figure can legitimately differ from its enclosing district's. Bavaria towns use 1951-2024; Austria towns use each station's own real start year through 2024 (Linz/Braunau effectively 1961, the SPARTACUS floor; Wels 1983; Salzburg 1987) — never backfilled earlier. hotDays is the 2015-2024 decade average, rounded to the nearest day. Full yearly/decade series and the exact methodology live in public/data/towns-climate.json; geoData.ts's literals are a baked snapshot of that file (re-run data-pipeline/scripts/process_town_climate.py and copy the new warming/hotDays values across if the underlying grids are ever updated).
methodNotes.openMeteoModelChoice: Phase 4 originally planned `models=era5_land` for the app's live Open-Meteo requests (src/hooks/useClimateData.ts, useAustriaData.ts) for its higher 9km resolution. Verified directly against the archive API first: era5_land returns `precipitation_sum: null` for every day tried, on any date range — confirmed before trusting it, not assumed from documentation. Plain `era5` (31km) was verified to return real values for both temperature and precipitation, so that's used instead; this keeps a single, consistent, explicitly-pinned model (not Open-Meteo's default era5_seamless blend, which can switch underlying sources across a time series without flagging it) without silently breaking precipitation. `?? 0` was removed from both files' response parsing — a day missing any of its four fields (temp max/min/mean, precipitation) is now dropped from the record array entirely rather than coerced to a fabricated zero; aggregateYearly/aggregateDecades (utils/aggregations.ts) were deliberately left untouched, since filtering at the point of ingestion means a missing day is simply absent from what reaches them, not a null threaded through every downstream average.
methodNotes.austriaNoSilentMixing: fetchAustriaDailyRange (useAustriaData.ts) now clips its own GeoSphere request to each town's real stationStartYear before calling it at all, rather than requesting the full caller-given range and letting GeoSphere's all-null response for pre-coverage years fall through to the Open-Meteo catch block. Verified directly: requesting station 145 (Salzburg) for 1950 returns tl_mittel as null for every day, not an error — if left to the generic catch-and-fallback, a request spanning e.g. 1950-2004 would silently hand the ENTIRE range to Open-Meteo on any transient GeoSphere hiccup, including the 1987-2004 years the station genuinely has real data for, quietly downgrading their provenance with no visible indication. Years before a station's real start are now simply never requested and stay absent from the result.
methodNotes.floodEventsNoData: TownData.floodEvents (useAppStore.ts) is `number | null`; all 11 towns in geoData.ts are currently null, not a hand-picked or fabricated count, until Phase 5 computes real values from GKD Bayern / eHYD gauge data. TownHeadline.tsx and the map tooltip (BavariaMap.tsx) both render an explicit 'not yet available' state instead of a number when null — the one necessary UI text change in Phase 4, per the explicit instruction that this field should show 'no data' until Phase 5 rather than continue displaying the old hand-typed counts.
